chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from Aban ibn Uthman from Abu al-Jaroud who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying, and he mentioned this Verse:
And We enjoined upon the human being [to be] good to his parents

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) is one of the two parents. So Abdullah ibn Ajlan said, 'Who is the other one?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Ali (peace be upon him), and his wives are prohibited unto us, and this is for us in particular.'
ai.seo_question: Who are the two parents mentioned in the interpretation of 'And We enjoined upon man goodness to his parents'?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi interprets the command for 'goodness to parents' (Birr al-Walidayn) as extending to the Prophet Muhammad and Imam Ali, establishing their spiritual parenthood. It further clarifies the unique status of the Prophet's wives, noting that while they are prohibited for others, they are exclusively permissible for the Ahl al-Bayt, a concept rooted in the verse of Purification and the Verse of Marriageability.
